arxiv-2011-12814.title: A Machine Learning Approach to Correcting Atmospheric Seeing in Solar Flare Observations 2020 A Machine Learning Approach to Correcting Atmospheric Seeing in Solar Flare Observations – References
arxiv-2011-12814.creator: John A. Armstrong, Lyndsay Fletcher
arxiv-2011-12814.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by John A. Armstrong, Lyndsay Fletcher. Current post-processing techniques for the correction of atmospheric seeing in solar observations – such as Speckle interferometry and Phase Diversity methods – have limitations when it comes to their reconstructive capabilities of solar flare observations. This, combined with the sporadic nature of flares meaning observers cannot wait until seeing conditions are optimal before taking measurements, means that many ground-based solar flare observations are marred with bad seeing.

arxiv-2305-07791.title: Using Deepfake Technologies for Word Emphasis Detection
arxiv-2305-07791.creator: Eran Kaufman, Lee-Ad Gottlieb
arxiv-2305-07791.description: Abstract In this work, we consider the task of automated emphasis detection for spoken language. This problem is challenging in that emphasis is affected by the particularities of speech of the subject, for example the subject’s accent, dialect or voice. To address this task, we propose to utilize deep fake technology to produce an emphasis-devoid speech for this speaker.

arxiv-2310-03432.title: Mitigating the Influence of Domain Shift in Skin Lesion Classification: A Benchmark Study of Unsupervised Domain Adaptation Methods on Dermoscopic Images
arxiv-2310-03432.creator: Sireesha Chamarthi, Katharina Fogelberg, Roman C. Maron, Titus J. Brinker, Julia Niebling
arxiv-2310-03432.description: Abstract The potential of deep neural networks in skin lesion classification has already been demonstrated to be on-par if not superior to the dermatologists’ diagnosis. However, the performance of these models usually deteriorates when the test data differs significantly from the training data (i.e. domain shift).

arxiv-2410-13399.title: Heisenberg scaling based on population coding
arxiv-2410-13399.creator: Masahito Hayashi
arxiv-2410-13399.description: Abstract We study Heisenberg scaling of quantum metrology in the viewpoint of population coding. Although Fisher information has been used for a figure of merit to characterize Heisenberg scaling in quantum metrology, several studies pointed out it does not work as a figure of merit because it does not reflect the global structure.

arxiv-2411-05371.title: BayesianFitForecast : A User-Friendly R Toolbox for Parameter Estimation and Forecasting with Ordinary Differential Equations
arxiv-2411-05371.creator: Hamed Karami, Amanda Bleichrodt, Ruiyan Luo, Gerardo Chowell
arxiv-2411-05371.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Hamed Karami, Amanda Bleichrodt, Ruiyan Luo, Gerardo Chowell. Mathematical models based on ordinary differential equations (ODEs) are essential tools across various scientific disciplines, including biology, ecology, and healthcare informatics where they are used to simulate complex dynamic systems and inform decision-making. In this paper, we introduce BayesianFitForecast , an R toolbox specifically developed to streamline Bayesian parameter estimation and forecasting in ODE models, making it particularly relevant to health informatics and public health decision-making ( https://github.com/gchowell/BayesianFitForecast/ ).

pmc-10654027.title: Novel_circ_003686 regulates the osteogenic differentiation of MSCs in patients with myeloma bone disease through miR-142-5p/IGF1 axis
pmc-10654027.creator: Ling Qiu, Lei Ma, Dan Chen, Nan Zhang, Jiao Cai, Qian Zhang, Xiao Wang, Hai Yi, Hao Yao, Fang-Yi Fan
pmc-10654027.description: Highlights•Circ_003686 was significantly under-expressed in MBD-BMSC. miR-142-5p was over-expressed in BMD-BMSC.•Overexpression of circ_003686 could significantly promoted osteogenic differentiation in BMD-BMSC.•Circ_003686 could bind miR-142-5p to promote osteogenic differentiation.•miR-142-5p could bind to IGF1 to promote osteogenic differentiation.•Circ_003686/miR-142-5p/IGF1 axis meaningfully controlled the relative expression ratios of PI3K/AKT pathway.

pmc-10736446.title: YOU JUST LEARN WHAT TO HOLD ON TO AND WHAT TO LET GO: NARRATIVES OF MINDFUL AGING IN SOUTH ASIAN AMERICAN OLDER ADULTS
pmc-10736446.creator: Mushira Khan, Ajla Basic
pmc-10736446.description: Mindful Sustainable Aging (MSA) is a multidimensional concept incorporating elements from four prominent gerontological theories – activity theory, disengagement theory, successful aging theory, and gerotranscendence theory (Nilsson et al., 2015). Informed by mindfulness practices, MSA is a holistic approach to supporting healthy aging in the social, physical, mental, and spiritual dimensions of life (ibid.).

pmc-11614611.title: Integrated multi-omics analyses combined with western blotting discovered that cis-TSG alleviated liver injury via modulating lipid metabolism
pmc-11614611.creator: Tekleab Teka, Jiang Wu, Patrick Kwabena Oduro, Ze Li, Chenxi Wang, Hao Chen, Lin Zhang, Haitao Wang, Liming Wang, Lifeng Han
pmc-11614611.description: Background: Polygonum multiflorum shows dual hepatoprotective and hepatotoxic effects. The bioactive components responsible for these effects are unknown. This study investigates whether cis-2,3,5,4'-tetrahydroxystilbene-2-O-β-D-glucoside (cis-TSG), a stilbene glycoside, has hepatoprotective and/or hepatotoxic effects in a liver injury model. Methods: C57BL/6J mice were administered α-naphthylisothiocyanate (ANIT) to induce cholestasis, followed by treatment with cis-TSG.

pmc-11644856.title: Satellite Fingerprinting Methods for GNSS Spoofing Detection
pmc-11644856.creator: Francisco Gallardo, Antonio Pérez-Yuste, Andriy Konovaltsev
pmc-11644856.description: Spoofing attacks pose a significant security risk for organizations and systems relying on global navigation satellite systems (GNSS) for their operations. While the existing spoofing detection methods have shown some effectiveness, these can be vulnerable to certain attacks, such as secure code estimation and replay (SCER) attacks, among others.

pmc-12714233.title: The effect of the modifiable areal unit problem on ecological model inference: A graphical simulation study for disease mapping in Australia
pmc-12714233.creator: James Hogg, Aiden Price, Conor Hassan, Shovanur Haque, Farzana Jahan, Wala Areed, Jessica Cameron, Susanna Cramb, Helen Thompson
pmc-12714233.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Statistical disease mapping is a valuable public health tool, as it identifies spatial patterns of disease occurrence. However, the Modifiable Areal Unit Problem (MAUP) poses challenges to disease mapping, as the aggregation of geographic units can impact statistical inferences. The effect of the MAUP depends on contextual factors, for example the geographic structure, aggregation level, choice of model, and the underlying data-generating process.

pmc-13342576.title: A synthetic dataset for time series super-resolution with deep learning
pmc-13342576.creator: Julio Ibarra-Fiallo, D’hamar Agudelo-Moreno, Juan A. Lara
pmc-13342576.description: The increasing application of time-series analysis in fields like biomedical engineering or telecommunications emphasizes the need for high-quality data to train and evaluate advanced machine learning models. Acquiring temporal data at suitable resolutions is often limited by ethical, economic, or practical constraints. We introduce CoSiBD (Complex Signal Benchmark Dataset for Super-Resolution), a synthetic dataset designed for reproducible time-series super-resolution research.
